name: Glitchy micro-loop buffer for ambient textures: freeze-and-scan buffer with segment length, pitch that cascades through feedback, temporary pitch from sample-rate steps, unlinked L/R (+12 / −12 st with cross feedback) and binary-random LFOs toggling freeze and reverse per side
goal: Recreate boutique 'micro-looper' pedal textures with one buffer-delay device. A delay whose position = delay time, feedback = repeats, and segment = how much of the capture plays, plus reverse and a hold/freeze that captures the buffer so position scans it. Add random start position (plus an LFO), a short range for finer control, pitch shift (an octave or a fifth; it cascades up with every feedback pass, so use the high-cut), sample-rate steps that create temporary pitch drops and crunch, vibrato, and a low/high-cut band-pass. Unlink L and R for independent positions, segments, pitch and LFOs: L +12 st, R −12 st with cross feedback. Then automate with binary (random on/off) LFOs at unequal rates on freeze L/R and on reverse L/R, plus a random LFO stepping the sample-rate/bandwidth, and optionally a hybrid reverb. Lower dry/wet for a background whisper. Delta vs our granular-freeze, reverb-freeze and shimmer skills: per-channel random binary freeze/reverse and octave-split cross feedback.

source.title: Ableton's best kept secret for ambient textures
source.transcript_note: Stock-device deep dive; route.py said COVERED but hand-check found per-channel binary freeze/reverse and cross-feedback not covered. Gumroad promo dropped.

prerequisites: Buffer/looper delay with freeze, position, segment, reverse, pitch, sample-rate and filter controls (Web Audio: AudioWorklet ring buffer with per-channel read heads, implementation note)
LFOs with binary-random and random shapes, mapped as remote (not manual) controls

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Melodic loop, keys or guitar-like part

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Pitch inside feedback cascades with each repeat: an octave (or a fifth) is plenty; two octaves gets shrill. Use the high-cut.
Sample-rate changes momentarily shift pitch (that's the effect); don't smooth them away.
Binary LFO rates on L vs R should differ so the channels don't freeze in sync.
Preset pack/promo in the source is omitted.

steps.action: Insert the buffer delay. Learn the basics: position = delay time, feedback = repeats, segment = how much of the captured audio plays back, reverse toggle.
steps.expect: Sounds like a delay at first

steps.action: Freeze/hold: play a phrase and engage hold. Now position scans through the frozen buffer and segment sets the loop length. Add random start position (and/or an LFO), and use short mode for fine, small segments.
steps.expect: Micro-loops scanned from the captured buffer

steps.action: Pitch: set +12 st (or a fifth). Each feedback pass pitches up again, so engage the high-cut to tame the cascading brightness. Try sample-rate steps (e.g. 10k, down an octave and again) for temporary pitch effects and crunch; add a little vibrato. Low and high cut together give band-pass tones.
steps.expect: Rising cascades and crunchy temporary drops

steps.action: Unlink L/R channels so each has its own position, segment, pitch and LFO. Set L +12 st and R −12 st, and set the feedback routing to cross (each side feeds the other).
steps.expect: Wide image; octaves interleave across channels

steps.action: Map the important controls to macros. Add two LFOs in binary (random on/off) mode at different rates on freeze L and freeze R, set as remote control so they aren't hand-moved.
steps.expect: Each channel freezes at random intervals

steps.action: Add two more binary LFOs on reverse L and reverse R, and one random (not binary) LFO with full range on the sample-rate/bandwidth control that steps between octave settings.
steps.expect: Random direction flips and octave jumps

steps.action: Optionally add a hybrid reverb, and lower dry/wet so the effect becomes a whisper in the background.
steps.expect: Evocative glitch texture under the dry part

verification: With hold on, changing position scans through the same captured audio.
Pitch +12 with feedback produces audibly rising repeats.
L and R freeze/reverse at different times when the binary LFOs run.
Stepping sample rate causes momentary pitch dips.
